<!-- Generated by cargo xtask docs. Do not edit. -->

You can use this page to read the JSON that rdy prints with `--json`, and know what each field means. The first section is the result of a run, which `rdy run --json` prints. The other sections cover the objects that `rdy verify --json`, `rdy spec lint --json` and `rdy version --json` print. The error object has a section too. rdy prints it with `--json` when it exits without a verdict.

In this release, `rdy run` and `rdy verify` are not built yet. With `--json`, each one prints the error object and exits 70. Their sections show the objects they will print.

Each table has one row per field. An object that more than one field names has one section. A row that names the same object links to that section.

The JSON report rdy writes and Rdy Cloud reads. Ignore fields you do not know. Accept values not listed where a description says Open. Use verdict as written. A whole document is at most 2 MiB; readers should check that before parsing.

## Top-level fields

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api_version` | one of `rdy/v1` | yes |  | Always `rdy/v1`. |  |
| `kind` | one of `Report` | yes |  | Always `Report`. |  |
| `producer` | object | yes |  | The rdy build that wrote this. |  |
| `run` | object | yes |  | When and how the run went. |  |
| `spec` | object | yes |  | Which spec ran. |  |
| `signature` | object | yes |  | Who signed the spec. |  |
| `host` | object | yes |  | The machine, coarsely. |  |
| `identity` | object | yes |  | Who ran it. |  |
| `proxy` | object or null | no | `null` | Proxy settings in effect, user info stripped. `null` when none. |  |
| `capabilities` | array of object | yes |  | Every need rdy probed before running checks, and the result. |  |
| `verdict` | one of `ready`, `ready_with_warnings`, `not_ready` | yes |  | The overall answer. Closed in v1: a new verdict value needs `rdy/v2`. Use it as written. |  |
| `verdict_reason` | one of `required_check_not_run`, `nothing_verified`, or another value or null | yes |  | Set when the verdict is not explained by an observed block or warning. `required_check_not_run` means NOT READY with no block. `nothing_verified` means READY with warnings because no check reached pass, warn or block. Otherwise `null`. Open. |  |
| `exit_code` | one of `0`, `1`, `2` | yes |  | The exit code for this verdict: 0, 1 or 2. When rdy cannot write the report it exits 70 instead and `complete` is false. |  |
| `summary` | object | yes |  | Counts of the results. |  |
| `checks` | array of object | yes |  | One entry per spec check, in spec order, at most 256. Sort by bucket for display. |  |
| `actions` | array of object | yes |  | Every file read, command, lookup, connection and API request, in order. At most 5000 entries. |  |
| `actions_truncated` | boolean | yes |  | `true` when the log dropped an entry: at the 5000 entry cap or a check's 1000 entry quota. `ok` then `failed` `read`, `read_dir`, `read_link` and `stat` entries go first. A `denied` entry is never dropped for another kind of entry, and repeated denials fold into one `coalesced` entry per parent directory (file calls) or per target (other calls). |  |
| `actions_dropped` | object | yes |  | How many entries of each kind were dropped. `read`, `read_dir`, `read_link`, `stat` and `coalesced` entries are dropped first; any other kind only as a last resort. |  |
| `redaction` | object | yes |  | What the redactor changed in this report. |  |
| `complete` | boolean | yes |  | `false` when rdy could not finish or write the report (exit 70). |  |
| `interrupted` | boolean | yes |  | `true` when the run was cancelled (Ctrl-C). |  |

## producer

The rdy build that wrote a report.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | one of `rdy` | yes |  | Always `rdy`. |  |
| `version` | string | yes |  | Version of the rdy binary. |  |
| `commit` | string or null | no | `null` | Short git commit of the build. |  |
| `rdy_spec` | string | yes |  | Version of the rdy-spec crate that wrote this file. |  |
| `target` | string | yes |  | Rust target triple. |  |

## run

When a run happened and the options it ran with.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  | Random UUID v4. |  |
| `started_at` | string | yes |  | UTC, with milliseconds. |  |
| `finished_at` | string | yes |  | UTC, with milliseconds. |  |
| `duration_ms` | integer | yes |  | Wall time of the run. |  |
| `options` | object | yes |  | The options that shaped the run. |  |

### options

The options of a run that change what a reader should expect.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs` | integer | yes |  | Checks that ran at once, 1 to 32. |  |
| `deadline_ms` | integer | yes |  | The run limit in milliseconds. |  |
| `allow_unsigned` | boolean | yes |  | Whether `--allow-unsigned` was set. |  |
| `network` | boolean | yes |  | `false` when sockets were turned off for this run. |  |
| `kube_context` | string or null | no | `null` | Context given with `--kube-context`, if any. |  |

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | string | yes |  | `metadata.product`. |  |
| `version` | string or null | no | `null` | `metadata.version`. |  |
| `sha256` | string | yes |  | SHA-256 of the exact bytes that were verified and parsed, 64 lowercase hex digits. |  |
| `file_name` | string | yes |  | Base name only, never the full path. |  |
| `size_bytes` | integer | yes |  | Size of the spec file. |  |
| `serial` | integer or null | no | `null` | `metadata.serial`. |  |
| `expires` | string or null | no | `null` | `metadata.expires`. |  |

| `annotations` | object | no | `{}` | `metadata.annotations`, at most 32. |  |

## signature

Who signed the spec, as far as rdy could tell.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | one of `verified`, `unsigned`, `invalid`, or another value | yes |  | `verified` is signed by a trusted key. `unsigned` is no signature, run with `--allow-unsigned`. `invalid` appears only in the `rdy verify` object, never in a report. Open: treat an unknown value as not verified. |  |
| `key_id` | string or null | no | `null` | Minisign key id, 16 uppercase hex digits. |  |
| `key_fingerprint` | string or null | no | `null` | SHA-256 of the 32 byte ed25519 public key, 64 hex digits. The key id alone is not an identity. |  |
| `product` | string or null | no | `null` | Product from the signed trusted comment. |  |
| `signed_at` | string or null | no | `null` | From the signed trusted comment. |  |
| `trust_note` | string or null | no | `null` | The local note from the trust store entry. Never text from the spec. |  |
| `trust_source` | one of `system`, `user`, `flag`, or another value or null | no | `null` | Where the key came from: the system or user trust store, or `flag` for a key given with `--key` for one run. Open: treat an unknown value like `flag`. |  |
| `reason` | string or null | no | `null` | For `invalid` only. |  |

The machine, coarsely. No MAC addresses, environment values, command line, working directory, home paths, kubeconfig contents, raw machine id or serial numbers.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hostname` | string | yes |  | As the OS reports it. |  |
| `host_id` | string or null | yes |  | First 16 hex digits of an HMAC-SHA256 of the OS machine id with key `rdy-host-id-v1` plus the product. The same host and product give the same value. Different products give unrelated values. `null` when there is no usable machine id (macOS for now). |  |
| `os` | object | yes |  | The operating system. |  |
| `kernel` | string or null | no | `null` | Kernel version. |  |
| `arch` | string | yes |  | CPU architecture. |  |
| `virtualization` | one of `none`, `vm`, `unknown`, or another value | no |  | Whether the host is a virtual machine. |  |
| `container` | boolean | no | `false` | rdy ran inside a container or WSL. |  |

The operating system of the host.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `family` | one of `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, or another value | yes |  | Linux, macOS or Windows. |  |
| `id` | string or null | no | `null` | Distribution id, such as `rhel`. |  |
| `version` | string or null | no | `null` | OS version. |  |

| `euid` | integer or null | yes |  | Effective uid on Unix, `null` on Windows. |  |

### kube

The Kubernetes identity of a run.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `context` | string or null | no | `null` | The kubeconfig context in use. |  |
| `server` | string or null | no | `null` | The API server URL. |  |
| `user` | string or null | no | `null` | The authenticated user from `SelfSubjectReview`. When that API is missing or the call fails, the user entry named in the kubeconfig context, with `user_verified` false. |  |
| `user_verified` | boolean | yes |  | `true` when `user` came from `SelfSubjectReview`. `false` when it is the kubeconfig user, which the API server did not verify. |  |

## capabilities entries

One thing rdy probed before running checks, such as root or a reachable cluster.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `need` | one of `root`, `kube_context`, `network`, `command`, `cloud_credentials`, or another value | yes |  | What was probed. |  |
| `name` | string or null | no | `null` | Program name for `command`, provider for `cloud_credentials`. |  |
| `available` | boolean | yes |  | Whether the need is met. |  |
| `detail` | string or null | no | `null` | For example `uid 1000` or `context acme-staging`. |  |
| `hint` | string or null | no | `null` | What to do when not available. |  |

## summary

Counts of the results.

`pass + warn + block + skipped + timeout + error = total` for every result whose status is known. `skipped` counts every `status: skipped` entry, not applicable included. `not_applicable`, `required_not_run` and `optional_not_run` are views inside that sum. A result whose status this version does not know counts in `total` and in `required_not_run` or `optional_not_run` only. The summary may gain keys, so never sum every key.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `total` | integer | yes |  | Number of results. |  |
| `pass` | integer | yes |  | Results with status `pass`. |  |
| `warn` | integer | yes |  | Results with status `warn`. |  |
| `block` | integer | yes |  | Results with status `block`. |  |
| `skipped` | integer | yes |  | Every result with status `skipped`, not applicable included. |  |
| `timeout` | integer | yes |  | Results with status `timeout`. |  |
| `error` | integer | yes |  | Results with status `error`. |  |
| `not_applicable` | integer | yes |  | Skipped because the spec's `os` list leaves this OS out. Never counts toward the verdict. |  |
| `required_not_run` | integer | yes |  | Severity block (or unknown) and not run. |  |
| `optional_not_run` | integer | yes |  | Severity warn and not run. |  |

## checks entries

The outcome of one check entry.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes |  | `id`, or `id/name` when the spec gave a name. Unique in the report. |  |
| `id` | string | yes |  | The check id. |  |
| `name` | string or null | yes | `null` | The spec's name for this entry, shown next to the id. |  |
| `family` | string | yes |  | The check family, such as `host`. |  |
| `severity` | one of `block`, `warn`, or another value | yes |  | From the spec. A value a consumer does not know counts as block. Open. |  |
| `status` | one of `pass`, `warn`, `block`, `skipped`, `timeout`, `error`, or another value | yes |  | After severity is applied. An unknown status counts as not run. Open. |  |
| `bucket` | one of `blocker`, `required_not_run`, `warning`, `passed`, `not_applicable`, or another value | yes |  | Display group, from the same rule as the verdict. Sort by it in this order: blocker, required_not_run, warning, passed, not_applicable. Do not recompute it. Open. |  |
| `skip_kind` | one of `missing_need`, `not_in_build`, `unknown_check`, `unsupported_spec`, `not_yet_on_os`, `not_applicable`, `run_deadline`, `cancelled`, or another value | no |  | Present when `status` is `skipped`. `not_applicable` comes only from the spec's `os` list. A check that cannot work on this OS is `not_yet_on_os`. Open. |  |
| `unsupported_fields` | array of string | no |  | For `unsupported_spec`: the fields this rdy could not read. |  |
| `timeout_after_ms` | integer | no |  | Present when `status` is `timeout`. |  |
| `error_kind` | one of `check_failed`, `panic`, or another value | no |  | Present when `status` is `error`. Open. |  |
| `message` | string | yes |  | One line, at most 1 KiB, such as `15.4 GiB found, 32 GiB needed`. |  |
| `fix` | string or null | yes | `null` | What to do. `null` only for pass and not applicable. |  |
| `fix_source` | one of `spec`, `rdy`, or another value or null | yes | `null` | Whose fix text `fix` is: `spec` is the vendor's text, `rdy` is rdy's own. `null` on pass. Open. |  |
| `builtin_fix` | string or null | no |  | rdy's text when the spec's fix replaced it. |  |
| `observed` | object or null | yes | `null` | Measured values, at most 64 KiB and 64 keys. Keys are per check id, in snake_case, with the unit in the name (`_bytes`, `_ms`, `_percent`). Keys are only ever added. A value is a scalar, or a list or object of at most three levels, with every text at most 4 KiB. |  |
| `expected` | object or null | yes | `null` | Thresholds that applied after defaults. Same rules as `observed`. |  |
| `needs` | array of object | yes |  | Hard and soft needs the check declared, and whether each was met. At most 32. |  |
| `partial` | object or null | yes | `null` | Set when some sources could not be read. A partial check never blocks on data it could not read. |  |
| `truncated` | boolean | yes |  | A size cap cut `message`, `fix`, `observed` or `expected`. |  |
| `notes` | array of string | yes |  | Up to 20 notes of 1 KiB each. |  |
| `started_ms` | integer | yes |  | Milliseconds after `run.started_at`. |  |
| `duration_ms` | integer | yes |  | How long the check took. |  |

### needs entries

A need a check declared and whether it was met.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `need` | one of `root`, `kube_context`, `network`, `command`, `cloud_credentials`, or another value | yes |  | What the check needs. |  |
| `name` | string or null | no | `null` | Program name for `command`, provider for `cloud_credentials`. |  |
| `hard` | boolean | yes |  | `true`: the check does not run without it. `false`: it runs partial. |  |
| `met` | boolean | yes |  | Whether it was available. |  |

### partial

Which sources a check could not read.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `missing` | array of one of `root`, `kube_context`, `network`, `command`, `cloud_credentials`, or another value | yes |  | The needs that were missing. |  |
| `missing_grants` | array of string | no | `[]` | Permissions the check lacked, one short text each, such as `list nodes` or `list csinodes (storage.k8s.io)`. Empty when the partial result has no such cause. Older reports omit it. |  |
| `note` | string | yes |  | What is missing, or the OS note for a `Partial` OS. |  |

## actions entries

One side effect, recorded as it happened. Fields beyond the required ones depend on kind.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seq` | integer | yes |  | Position in the log, from 1. |  |
| `check` | string or null | yes |  | Check key, or `null` for run level probes. |  |
| `at_ms` | integer | yes |  | Milliseconds after `run.started_at`. |  |
| `duration_ms` | integer | yes |  | How long it took. |  |
| `kind` | one of `exec`, `read`, `read_dir`, `read_link`, `stat`, `env`, `lookup`, `connect`, `tls`, `http`, `dns`, `kube`, `native`, `coalesced`, or another value | yes |  | What kind of effect. |  |
| `outcome` | one of `ok`, `denied`, `failed`, `timeout`, or another value | yes |  | How it ended. |  |
| `rule` | string | no |  | For a denied call, the rule that refused it. Absent otherwise. |  |
| `error` | string | no |  | Why the call failed, as a fixed phrase. Absent otherwise. |  |
| `program` | string | no |  | exec |  |
| `argv` | array of string | no |  | exec, after redaction |  |
| `exit` | integer or null | no |  | exec |  |
| `stdout_bytes` | integer | no |  | exec |  |
| `path` | string | no |  | read, read_dir, read_link, stat, native, kube. Paths under a home directory start with ~. For read_link it is the link, never what the link points to. |  |
| `bytes` | integer | no |  | read, connect (the udp reply), http (the unix socket body) |  |
| `entries` | integer | no |  | read_dir |  |
| `name` | string | no |  | env (the name only, never the value), dns |  |
| `host` | string | no |  | lookup, connect, tls |  |
| `answers` | integer | no |  | lookup |  |
| `port` | integer | no |  | connect |  |
| `addr` | string or null | no |  | connect: the IP address used. |  |
| `proto` | one of `udp` | no |  | connect: udp for a datagram exchange. Absent for a TCP connection. |  |
| `via_proxy` | string or null | no |  | connect, kube: the proxy origin with the user info stripped, or null for a direct request |  |
| `sni` | string | no |  | tls |  |
| `header` | string | no |  | kube: name of the refused request header, never its value |  |
| `impersonated` | boolean | no |  | kube: true when the request was sent with Impersonate-User, as the spec's `as` user. Absent otherwise. Never the user name. |  |
| `kubeconfig_impersonates` | boolean | no |  | kube: true on the run-level `GET /version` when the kubeconfig user sets an `as`, `as-uid`, `as-groups` or `as-user-extra` field, so kube adds Impersonate headers to every request. Absent otherwise. Never the user name. |  |
| `method` | string | no |  | http, kube |  |
| `url` | string | no |  | http, without query string |  |
| `status` | integer or null | no |  | http, kube |  |
| `server` | string | no |  | dns: the nameserver's IP address. |  |
| `rtype` | string | no |  | dns |  |
| `api` | string | no |  | native, for example statvfs |  |
| `of` | string | no |  | coalesced: the kind that was coalesced |  |
| `under` | string | no |  | coalesced: the parent directory the file calls were under, or the program, host or path the other denied calls named, or * for denied calls past 100 targets |  |
| `count` | integer | no |  | coalesced: how many calls the entry stands for. Reads past 200 per directory, or denied calls and failed file calls past 20 per parent directory (file calls) or target (other denied calls) and reason. |  |
| `truncated` | boolean | no |  | exec, read, connect (udp), http (unix socket) |  |

## Error output with --json

Not a report. What rdy prints on stdout with --json when it exits 64 or 70 without a verdict. api_version and kind are written but not required.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api_version` | one of `rdy/v1` | no |  | Always `rdy/v1`. |  |
| `kind` | one of `Error` | no |  | Always `Error`. |  |
| `error` | object | yes |  | What went wrong, and what to do next. |  |
| `verdict` | null | yes |  | Always null. No verdict was reached. |  |
| `complete` | one of `false` | yes |  | Always false. No complete report was written. |  |

### error

What went wrong, and what to do next.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | Stable code: usage, spec_unreadable, spec_parse, spec_invalid, spec_unsigned, spec_signature_invalid, spec_key_unknown, spec_expired, trust_store_insecure, report_write, interrupted, internal. Open. |  |
| `message` | string | yes |  | What went wrong, in words. |  |
| `fix` | string | yes |  | What to do next. |  |
| `file` | string or null | no |  | The file the error is about, or null. |  |
| `line` | integer or null | no |  | The line in that file, from 1, or null. |  |
| `column` | integer or null | no |  | The column in that line, from 1, or null. |  |

## rdy spec lint --json

Not a `Report`. What `rdy spec lint` prints with `--json`.

The counts equal the number of findings of each level.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api_version` | one of `rdy/v1` | yes |  | Always `rdy/v1`. |  |
| `kind` | one of `Lint` | yes |  | Always `Lint`. |  |
| `file` | string | yes |  | The file as the caller named it. |  |
| `findings` | array of object | yes |  | Every finding, in file order. Empty when the spec is clean. A spec has at most 256 check entries and each gives at most one finding, and the file itself gives at most two (a parse error, an expired spec), so there are never more than 258. |  |
| `errors` | integer | yes |  | How many findings are errors. |  |
| `warnings` | integer | yes |  | How many findings are warnings. |  |

### findings entries

One finding of a `LintReport`.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | one of `warning`, `error` | yes |  | Warning or error. |  |
| `code` | one of `unknown_key`, `unknown_check`, `unsupported_field`, `bad_value`, `not_in_build`, `no_threshold`, `structure`, or another value | yes |  | The code: `unknown_key`, `unknown_check`, `unsupported_field`, `bad_value`, `not_in_build`, `no_threshold` or `structure`. The set only grows. |  |
| `line` | integer or null | no |  | The line in the file, from 1, when it is known. |  |
| `column` | integer or null | no |  | The column in the file, from 1, when it is known. |  |
| `key` | string or null | no |  | The key of the check the finding is about (`host.disk` or `host.disk/data`). Null for a finding about the file as a whole. |  |
| `message` | string | yes |  | What is wrong. Safe to print: text from the file is cut and escaped. |  |
| `fix` | string | yes |  | What to do about it. Never empty. |  |

## rdy version --json

The `rdy` binary's own identity, as `rdy version --json` prints it.

Like the other `rdy/v1` objects it only grows: a later release may add fields, and a reader ignores the ones it does not know. `commit` and `date` are `null` when the build had no trustworthy git information, for example a build from a source tarball.

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | one of `rdy` | yes |  | Always `rdy`. |  |
| `version` | string | yes |  | Version of the rdy binary, such as `0.1.0` or `0.1.0-alpha.3`. |  |
| `commit` | string or null | yes |  | Short git commit of the build: the first 7 hex digits of the hash. |  |
| `date` | string or null | yes |  | Date of that commit in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |  |
| `target` | string | yes |  | Rust target triple the binary was built for. |  |
| `rdy_spec` | string | yes |  | Version of the rdy-spec crate inside this binary. |  |
| `api_version` | one of `rdy/v1` | yes |  | The wire format this binary reads and writes. Always `rdy/v1` in this release line. |  |
